event.description:
As the leaves begin to fall and the seasons begin to change, Missoula’s most spine-chilling history starts to emerge. Step into the shadows and uncover Missoula’s haunted past. This chilling tour weaves together stories of forgotten stories, abandoned buildings, and even tales of murder, bringing the darker side of the city’s history to life.

The walking tour begins in front of the flagpole and fountain at First Interstate Bank, and lasts approximately 90 minutes. Since this is a Halloween tour, we recommend dressing warmly for the cool evening air. Comfortable walking shoes are a must, and while costumes are optional, they’re always encouraged to add to the spirit of the evening! This experience is recommended for ages 12 and up.

In partnership with Cranky Sam, each ticket includes a limited-edition Screams & Spirits sticker and a special coupon for a Cranky Sam brewing product.

Cash tips are always appreciated by our guides, but never expected.

event.title: 2026 Downtown Missoula Fall Alley Pop-Up
event.description:
The Downtown Missoula Partnership is hosting its third Alley Pop-Up event with a fall harvest theme! Join us on October 2nd in the alley between Toiffer and Rice Thai in Downtown Missoula from 4:30–7:30 PM for a cozy autumnal activation. This event will truly add some fall colors to your October First Friday!

This event will include:

  • Fall-themed decor — we’re talking lights, hay bales, pumpkins, corn stalks, and more! 🎃
  • Jammin’ music from DJ TRX 🎶
  • Heaters to keep you warm🔥
  • Select fall treats and food options🍎
  • Bar hosted by the Rhino with fall-themed cocktails, mocktails, beer, wine, and more! 🍹

We hope you can join us to catch some fall vibes in Downtown Missoula!

A huge thank you to the local businesses allowing this pop-up to happen, and to ACE Hardware for sponsoring this event!

event.title: From Past to Plate: Downtown Historic Tour + Dining 1889
event.description:
Step back in time with an exclusive Unseen Missoula historic walking tour. Discover hidden stories as you wander the streets of Downtown with expert guides. Then, enjoy a curated fine dining experience that beautifully blends history and flavor. It’s not just a meal – it’s a journey through time, with the opportunity to connect with your community and support what you love about Downtown.

Connect with fellow supporters and learn about the Missoula Downtown Foundation’s latest projects and initiatives. Towards the end of the event, there will be an opportunity to make a meaningful donation that will directly support the enhancement of Downtown through the vibrancy of arts and culture, livability, economy, and safety.

Hotels and Hooligans Tour

Daily life and culture in Missoula during the city’s railroad boom—the Hotels and Hooligans tour looks at how the average Missoulian (whether long-time or just passing through) lived and recreated. Scandals and other sketchiness from the Courthouse to the seedy underbelly of Missoula’s railroad hotel district will also be revealed!

6:30pm – Hotels and Hooligans Tour

Meet promptly at 6:30pm across from the XXX’s sculpture on North Higgins at the Burlington Northern Plaza

7:30pm – Dinner at 1889

Appetizer – smoked Idaho trout tostada, benne seed lavash, Flathead cherry gastrique, creamy horseradish, crispy trout skin and chervil
Main – Marbled Meat Co. 8oz sirloin, local elderberry demiglace, wilted spinach, roasted garlic mashed potatoes
Dessert – salted honey & brown butter bar, Montana honey with whipped Amalthea goat cheese
Beverage – glass of house wine or pint of beer

(vegetarian option upon request)

Basements and Back Alleys Historic Tour

A holistic look at downtown life during Missoula’s transition from a marginal frontier town to a major local economic and cultural center from 1880 to 1920. The tour starts at Caras Park and lasts approximately 90 minutes. These less-accessible spaces remain hidden the majority of the year, so catch them while you can…

event.title: Navigating the Genderverse Workshop
event.description:
Navigating the Genderverse Workshop | TransVisible Montana

This presentation is created and facilitated by TransVisible Montana collective members with the intention of creating a “brave space” for folks to gain education regarding the challenges that misinformation and cisnormative systems create for transgender, non-binary, and Two-Spirit Montanans.

Participants will learn what support is helpful in overcoming challenges and will be engaged in activities and discussions that deepen their understanding and comfort with pronouns and their use in introductions.

Participants will explore gender as a part of the human experience that expands beyond the gender binary, and identify effective and ineffective allyship qualities.

Participants will have the opportunity to collect TransVisible Montana resources such as posters, stickers, cards, and handouts that will be helpful in the continued practice of their newly acquired knowledge and allyship skills.

Outcomes Include:

  • A broadened awareness & practice of contemporary, inclusive language.
  • Applicable skills & ideas for work, home, school & public environments.
  • Permission for liberation from the gender binary!

Connect with fellow supporters and learn about the Missoula Downtown Foundation’s latest projects and initiatives. Towards the end of the event, there will be an opportunity to make a meaningful donation that will directly support the enhancement of Downtown through the vibrancy of arts and culture, livability, economy, and safety.

Bricks and Brothels Historic Tour

While most in Missoula are familiar with the name Mary Gleim or the brief history of Front Street, many of the district’s stories remain untold including Gleim’s and her businesses. Since its existence along the historic Mullan Road, Front Street has been dubbed with the title of Missoula’s ‘red light district’ implicating that district remained a place of vice, sin, and corruption influenced by the radical reformist religious movements of the late 19th century. However, violence and addiction found throughout the entirety of the American West remain only a sliver of the true story.

From 1889-1917, West Front and Main Streets became home to a vibrant ‘restricted’ community of working women, Chinese laborers, African American soldiers, and immigrants who built the environment we as Missoulians have come to love today. This tour discusses the district through the historical lenses of sex, race, class, and occupation in order to create a broader social understanding against the backdrop of the remaining built environment.

AI for Small Business: Practical Tools, Real Applications

Discover how small businesses are using AI today, explore accessible tools, and identify opportunities that could save time, increase productivity, and support your goals.
November 19, 4-6 pm
Location: GoodWorks Place, 129 W. Alder

Downtown Dialogues is a community conversation series that brings together local business owners, leaders, and neighbors to share stories, ideas, and perspectives shaping Downtown Missoula. Each event features candid discussions around timely topics—from growth and resilience to creativity and collaboration—designed to spark connection, learning, and meaningful dialogue. Downtown Dialogues is co-hosted with the Downtown Missoula Partnership & Missoula Economic Partnership and sponsored by First Security Bank.
